note: The main banks, chosen as the best-known large card issuers (no central bank ranking was read): Arab Bank, the Housing Bank and Capital Bank. Arab Bank Jordan's card pages give no prices and its fees page links no card tariff (its Reflect digital bank's card, read on 2026-10-29, is kept); the Housing Bank's site didn't answer this research's connections; Bank al Etihad's fees manual (7 October 2026) answered with a CloudFront block and wasn't read. Reflect, Arab Bank's digital bank in Jordan: its fees and commissions charge its credit card 1.5% a month in interest and nothing to apply for or issue, with no yearly fee among them. Capital Bank's rates and fees (the July 2026 edition, read in full on 2026-10-30): its credit cards in dinars, each free for its first year and then charged its primary card's annual renewal fee (Visa Platinum 50, Signature 70, Infinite 150, Infinite Privilege 500 dinars), waived when the year's purchases reach 2,000, 4,000, 6,000 or 10,000 dinars; its Visa Infinite in US dollars, euros, pounds, dirhams and riyals, each with its issuance or annual fee (200 dollars, euros or pounds; 750 dirhams or riyals), waived on a year's purchases of 15,000 dollars or pounds, 35,000 euros or 55,000 dirhams or riyals. Every card bears 1.5% a month on the outstanding balance; a cash advance costs 4%, at least 4 dinars (the floor written on the dinar cards only); the foreign currency conversion fee is 3% for all currencies and 4% for euro transactions (written as 3%, the game's card holding one share); the overline fee and the late payment fee are each 10 dinars a month, written on the dinar cards (on the foreign-currency cards a fee set in dinars isn't written). The fee for paying in dinars at a merchant abroad (1.5%) isn't written. The schedule states no minimum payment or grace period. Wave 4 (2026-10-30): Cairo Amman Bank was added, a large Jordanian card issuer whose commission sheet answers this research (the Housing Bank's site again didn't answer; Jordan Ahli Bank's fees page linked no card tariff; Bank al Etihad wasn't retried). Its commission sheet (English, undated, the one its interest rates, commissions and fees page links), the credit Mastercard rows, read in full: each primary card's annual renewal fee (Standard and Preferred 25 dinars, priced as one row and written as one card; Titanium and Platinum 50, likewise; World 75; World Elite 120), written as a yearly fee (the sheet's issuance-fee exemptions name the bank's employees and Signature clients, conditions the game doesn't check); interest of 1.5% a month on the unpaid used balance for the bank's clients; a cash withdrawal commission on a credit Mastercard of 4% with a minimum of 5 dinars; a late payment commission of 10 and a commission of 10 for exceeding the limit; and a 3% mark-up on amounts used in a foreign currency. The Multi Currency credit card's two rows (120 to issue and renew, and 75 to renew) disagree and it isn't written; the World for Business card isn't personal. The sheet states no minimum payment or grace period. Wave 5 (2026-10-30), minimum payments: Reflect's support page gives its credit card's minimum payment as 5% of the amount a month, 15 dinars at least, written as 5% with a floor of 15. No minimum payment is published for Capital Bank's or Cairo Amman Bank's cards; tried: Capital Bank's four credit card pages (read 2026-10-30: instalment plans and limits, no minimum) and its rates and fees, Cairo Amman Bank's card pages (a Cloudflare check) and its commission sheet (no minimum), the Central Bank of Jordan (searches in English and Arabic found no rule setting one), and archive.org's API (a snapshot of Capital Bank's Platinum page of 23 June 2026, which this research's connection can't open; none of Cairo Amman Bank's cards page).
